content.text: Root cause: `to_cents` truncates (`int(19.99*100)` = 1998). Fix with rounding via Decimal for exactness.

content.text:
Fixed. `to_cents` in `ledger/currency.py` was truncating floats with `int(amount * 100)`. In floating point, `19.99 * 100` is `1998.9999…`, so it came out as 1998 cents. It now converts through `Decimal(str(amount))` and rounds half up. All 5 tests pass, including the report tests.

`str(amount)` uses the shortest decimal form of the float, so `19.99` becomes exactly `19.99`. Amounts with more than two decimal places are rounded half up to the nearest cent. Negative amounts also round half up, which means toward positive infinity (`-0.125` becomes -12 cents, not -13). I didn't check whether you want a different rule for negatives.
